full_judgment:
7. Mr Santi Ranjan Karmaker, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Court of appeal below erred in law in reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court without properly adverting to the reasons assigned by it. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Court of appeal below erred in law in deciding the question of limitation in a casual manner without properly discussing and considering the evidence on this point and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr Karmaker further submits that the learned appellate Court also erred in law in holding that the suit is bad for misjoinder of parties as well as for misjoinder of causes of action and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 9. The learned District Judge found that questions of law and facts involved in the present case for petitioner No. 1 are not common to petitioner No. 2 and as such, filing of the case jointly by them is hit by the provision of Order 1 rule (11) of the Code of Civil Procedure and on that ground the case is liable to be dismissed. It appears from the record that this plea of mis-joinder of the parties and mis-joinder of causes of action were not specifically taken by the pre-emptees in their written objection. It also appears from the record that no issue was framed on this point. In this case, it is an undisputed fact that the kabala under pre-emption is an un-divided single document. Petitioner No.1 claims pre-emption on the basis of inheritance as well as on the basis of holding land contiguous to the case land while pre-emptor-petitioner No.2 claims pre-emption as a contiguous land-holder. Although the basis of claim of the petitioners is not the same, nonetheless one is not mutually exclusive of the other and these claims are not contradictory as well. Moreover, filing of the pre-emption case by the petitioners in respect of an undivided single document does not in any way prejudice the pre-emptees. Mr Karmaker in support of his contention has referred to the case of Matilal Sikder and others vs. Benodini Dasi reported in 28 DLR (AD) 5 wherein their-Lordships held that a suit cannot be defeated by reason of mis-joinder or non-joinder of parties and objection as to non-joinder or mis-joinder of parties must be taken at the earliest opportunity. Their Lordships further held that the question of maintainability of a suit has to be taken before the framing of the issues and if not so taken it must be presumed to have been waived. In the instant case, it appears that no meaningful objection on the point of maintainability of the case was raised before the trial Court and no such issue was framed. In the facts and circumstances of the case it appears that the learned Court of appeal below was not justified in holding that the case is bad for mis-joinder of parties. The contention of Mr Karmaker on this point succeeds. But since the pre-emptors have failed to prove that they filed the pre-emption case within the time prescribed by law they are not entitled to any relief as prayed for. Since the judgment of the learned Court of appeal below does not suffer from any legal infirmity and it is based on evidence on record, I find no scope to interfere with the impugned decision, which has not occasioned failure of justice.
